Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
Comments: 2 active IXPs CAS-IX FEZIX moderate participation
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Verified directly via PCH, PeeringDB and Internet Society Pulse (current 2026 data): both CAS-IX (Casablanca, established 2019, 3 peers, 30G capacity) and FEZIX (Fez, 3 peers, 210G capacity) are active and operational. Two functioning IXPs supports Value 4 ('Active IXP(s)'), though participant counts at each (3 peers) are modest — bordering on 'limited participation' (Level 3). Confirmed at Value 4 but flagged as borderline for human review.
